cohort: The study included 10,565 very low birth weight (VLBW) infants, 24-30 weeks' gestational age, born alive without major congenital anomalies between 2013 and 2016, from seven countries participating in the Spanish SEN1500 and South American NEOCOSUR neonatal networks.
finding: Perinatal results continue to be more favorable for VLBW female infants compared to males in the context of current perinatology, with female infants exhibiting lower rates of respiratory distress syndrome, necrotizing enterocolitis, major brain damage, and moderate-severe BPD, and higher rates of survival and survival without morbidity.
